overview.summary: South Korea offers degree programmes and Korean-language programmes at universities, with government GKS scholarships for a small number of Nepali applicants each year. Work rights depend on your programme, your TOPIK level and your university’s status.
overview.educationSystem: Four-year bachelor’s degrees, two-year master’s and doctoral programmes, plus university-run Korean language institutes. Many degree programmes are taught in Korean; English-taught options are more common at graduate level.

studentVisa.category: D-2 student visa / D-4 language trainee visa
process: Prepare verified academic documents and financial evidence.
Book an online appointment with the embassy.
Submit originals and copies as required.
Register for an alien registration card after arrival.

financialEvidence.requirement: You must show a bank balance certificate and recent statements covering your study costs. The Embassy of Korea in Nepal asks for statements from an “A level” bank and original documents. The minimum amount varies by programme and university; confirm it with the embassy and your university before applying.

insurance.requirement: International students generally must join National Health Insurance.

documents: Balance certificate and 6 months of bank statements
Invitation letter and letter of guarantee where requested
NOC from Nepal’s Ministry of Education

conditions: Part-time work needs prior permission from the immigration office.

Allowed hours depend on your degree level, TOPIK score and the university’s certification status (for example up to 25 weekday hours for some undergraduates with TOPIK 3 at certified universities, less in other cases). Check the current rule with the official source before relying on this.
Language-programme (D-4) students generally have tighter limits. Check the current rule with the official source before relying on this.
Unauthorised work can lead to fines and deportation. Part-time income is limited and should not be used to plan tuition.

postStudyRoutes.conditions: For graduates actively looking for work. Paid work is generally not allowed on D-10 except approved internships. Check the current rule with the official source before relying on this.

postStudyRoutes.name: E-7 specific activities visa
postStudyRoutes.conditions: Requires a job offer in an eligible professional occupation.

lifestyle.text: University dormitories are affordable. Private one-room apartments often need a large key deposit.
Fast, cheap subways, buses and high-speed trains.
Four distinct seasons: hot, humid summers and cold, dry winters.
International students generally must join National Health Insurance.
Very safe cities. Learn basic Korean for daily life and work.
